title: Harness Studio app manifest
description:
The `app.json` contract for a Harness Studio app. Every field here is read by the host: `lib/manifest.mjs` validates it at load time and the normalized result is what `lib/backends.mjs`, `lib/proxy.mjs` and `lib/static.mjs` act on. A capability the host does not enforce does not belong in this file.

This document is the EDITOR-facing contract and is deliberately stricter than the runtime validator: `additionalProperties` is false so a typo gets a squiggle while you write, whereas the runtime reports an unknown key as a warning and still loads the app, so a manifest written against a newer schema does not brick an older host.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this file, so editors resolve completions without configuration.

schemaVersion.description: The manifest contract version. The host refuses a version it does not implement rather than guessing at the shape.

name.description: Unique kebab-case identifier. It appears in URLs (`/apps/<name>/api/*`), in the data home path, and as a React key, so the charset is bounded. Names the host's own routes own are reserved.

version.description: Semver. Compared on update, so a non-semver string is refused rather than sorted as text.

displayName.description: Human-readable name, shown in the app list and the page header.

description.description: One paragraph on what the app does and what it can reach.

defaultEnabled.description: Whether the app is on the first time the host sees it. An explicit enable/disable always wins over this; it only decides the undecided state.

ui.description: Surfaces the app OWNS. Absent means a headless app: a backend and no page.

entry.description: ESM entry relative to the app's `ui/` directory, served at `/apps/<name>/ui/<entry>` under `default-src 'none'; sandbox`. The file must exist at load time.

export.description: The named export the host calls as `mount(container, sdk)`.

pages.description: Routes this app's entry renders. Without at least one page nothing navigates to the entry.

route.description: Absolute path the page owns. `/` is refused: an app routed at the root would swallow the whole shell.

icon.description: Icon name resolved by the shell's icon set. An unknown name renders a fallback rather than failing the page.

backend.description: The app's own HTTP process. Absent means no process: `/apps/<name>/api/*` answers 502 and nothing is spawned. Declared here rather than discovered by file presence, so the manifest cannot disagree with what actually runs.

kind.description: Runtime the host spawns the entry with.

entry.description: Script relative to the app root. The file must exist at load time — a manifest naming a backend that is not there is refused, not silently ignored.

healthCheck.description: Unsigned liveness route the host polls before publishing the proxy. It is the ONLY route a backend may answer without the proxy HMAC.

maxBodyBytes.description: Ceiling on a proxied request body. The proxy HMAC covers the body, so the bytes are buffered before they are forwarded — without a ceiling one upload is one out-of-memory. A larger body is refused with 413.

startupTimeoutMs.description: How long the host waits for the health route after spawn before reporting the backend unhealthy.

restart.description: What the host does when the process exits on its own.

capabilities.description: What the host lets the app reach. Every field here is ENFORCED by the host — which is also why the list is short. A backend is an ordinary child process, so anything the host cannot actually withhold (outbound network, filesystem reach) is deliberately absent rather than declared and unpoliced; it comes back when there is a sandbox to enforce it. Every app gets `<home>/apps/<name>/data` and no declaration is needed for it.

inbound.description: Whether the host proxies `/apps/<name>/api/*` into the backend at all. `false` makes the proxy answer 403 without touching the process.

events.description:
The app's event vocabulary: every name that may cross the host/app boundary, in either direction (the host pushing state down, the entry reporting a selection up). `createEventBus({allowed})` refuses `on()` for anything outside it, so a typo is a loud refusal rather than a listener that waits forever.

Enforced only when the embedding shell passes the list to `createAppSdk({allowedEvents})`. The validator warns when an app declares events, so an author is never left assuming a guarantee the shell has not opted into.

forwardHeaders.description: Request headers the proxy copies from the browser into the backend. Default-deny: an app backend is third-party code behind an HMAC hop and gets its own identity, so the host's own credentials never cross it. `cookie`, `authorization`, `proxy-authorization` and the proxy signature header itself are refused outright.

contributes.description:
Rows the app adds to surfaces the HOST renders. Separate from `ui`, which is where an app declares surfaces of its own — the split is what lets an app with no page still reach the launcher.

Status: validated and published on `GET /api/apps`, not yet rendered by the Studio shell. The validator says so in a warning rather than letting a declaration vanish silently.

sessionControls.description: Compact controls rendered inside the composer, on the path of every turn — capped so one app cannot crowd the bar out. An app needing more configuration has a page for it.

entry.description: ESM bundle relative to `ui/`, lazily imported like a page.

statusPath.description: Route WITHIN the app's own backend reporting `{state, tooltip}` for the chip before it is opened. Deliberately not a URL — no scheme, no host, no query — so a control cannot point the poll at another origin. The host prefixes the app's own API base itself.

os.description: Platforms the app runs on. The host warns at load time when the current platform is not listed; it does not hide the app, because a manifest is not a better judge of the machine than the machine.
